description: Five manually bounded primitive-retrieval tasks derived from real public GitHub issues, with source snapshots separated from model-visible requests and independently authored hidden cases.
claim_limitations: This is not a full coding benchmark and does not measure issue resolution or patch generation.
The five tasks are a manually selected positive workload and are not a representative sample of GitHub issues.
Each request deliberately bounds an issue-derived need to one capability implemented by the current eleven-primitive catalog.
Unsupported-task abstention is not scored because the version-one executable-case contract has no must-abstain oracle disposition.

tasks.request: Remove duplicate finite JSON values from a sequence while preserving the first-seen order of each distinct value, including structurally equal records.

source_provenance.issue_title: DOC/TST: is pd.unique and the order it returns API?
source_provenance.source_excerpt: Note that `Series.unique()` and `unique()` return values in order of appearance.
source_provenance.derivation_scope: The task isolates stable first-occurrence deduplication; pandas Series/Index typing and API documentation are outside this retrieval case.

tasks.request: Split an in-memory sequence of database rows into deterministic contiguous upload batches of a positive requested size, keeping a smaller final batch without repeating rows.

source_provenance.issue_title: ichunked function iterator does not iterate when I'm trying to split Cassandra results
source_provenance.source_excerpt: The iterator of iterators that `ichunked` returned new and new sub-iterators with same and same contents.
source_provenance.derivation_scope: The task covers finite contiguous batching and no-repeat output; Cassandra access, laziness, concurrency, and the reported library regression are excluded.

tasks.request: Flatten one nested JSON event object into a single-level record using an explicit path separator while retaining its leaf values.

source_provenance.issue_title: Feature suggestion: flexible hierarchical data (json) importer (will implement if interest exists)
source_provenance.source_excerpt: I recently wrote a very flexible module for flattening hierarchical (json) data into CSV.
source_provenance.derivation_scope: The task covers recursive mapping-key flattening only; list explosion, pattern languages, CSV conversion, indexes, and DataFrame construction are excluded.

tasks.request: Scale a non-empty finite numeric feature vector so its minimum becomes zero and maximum becomes one, with a constant vector deterministically mapped to zeros.

source_provenance.issue_title: `MinMaxScalar.fit_transform()` Returns Zero When All Elements Are Same
source_provenance.source_excerpt: If all elements in a column are the same, the scaler transforms these elements to zeros.
source_provenance.derivation_scope: The task adopts the issue's observed zero-for-constant behavior for one vector; multi-column estimator APIs, fit state, and alternate feature ranges are excluded.

tasks.request: Standardize a non-empty finite numeric vector with its population mean and population variance, returning a zero vector when the population variance is zero.

source_provenance.issue_title: _handle_zeros_in_scale causing improper scaling when using StandardScaler()
source_provenance.source_excerpt: Expected both scaled results to be zero vector since both are constant-valued vectors.
source_provenance.derivation_scope: The task covers one-vector population z-score behavior and the constant-vector boundary; estimator state, sparse arrays, and tolerance policy are excluded.
